events.name: UT Opera Theatre presents "The Crucible"
events.info: A gripping return to Salem?s charged world of accusation and conscience, centering on John and Elizabeth Proctor?s moral stand. This operatic interpretation of Arthur Miller's timely play fuses lyrical intensity with sharp, speech-driven drama. An American classic that earned the Pulitzer Prize for Music, UTOT is thrilled to revisit this powerful work, last seen on our stage in 2009 and 2017, performed by two talented casts and an orchestra of University of Tennessee Opera Theatre students.
events.pleaseNote: Please note that balcony-level seating is accessible only by stairs; there is no elevator access to the balcony level. THIS IS A GENERAL ADMISSION EVENT. We reserve the right to revoke tickets sold through brokers or unauthorized third parties. If your ticket is revoked, you will not be admitted and will not receive a refund. Event date, time, and supporting acts are subject to change. All sales are final. No refunds or exchanges. Tickets will be available approximately 24 hours before the event.

boxOfficeInfo.openHoursDetail: Bijou Theatre doors typically open one hour prior to showtime and tickets can be purchased at Will Call. Advance tickets can be purchased from the Tennessee Theatre Box Office during business hours
boxOfficeInfo.willCallDetail: Will Call can be picked up inside the Bijou Theatre lobby the day of the performance typically one hour prior to the performance. Please have photo ID ready for ticket retrieval.

venues.parkingDetail: Several parking lots and on-street metered spaces are located within walking distance of the Bijou Theatre. The closest parking is a pay lot, Republic Parking, next to the venue on Cumberland. venues.accessibleSeatingDetail: The Bijou Theatre has ADA seating in the lower level only. The venue does not have an elevator to the balcony level. For more information, please call the Bijou Theatre at 865-522-0832.

generalInfo.generalRule: Weapons of any kind, including pocketknives; outside food and beverages; smoking of any kind, including e-cigarettes; illegal substances; professional or flash photography, tripods, selfie-sticks; backpacks, bags, oversized purses, etc. are prohibited at the venue. events.name: Broadway at the Tennessee: Death Becomes Her
events.info: Some people will do anything to look eternally fabulous. But famous actress Madeline Ashton and her best frenemy Helen Sharp are about to go too far... thanks to a mysterious woman named Viola Van Horn and a secret potion that's to die for. DEATH BECOMES HER is the Tony Award® -winning drop-dead hilarious new musical comedy based on the classic 1992 film with direction and choreography by Tony winner Christopher Gattelli. DEATH BECOMES HER is "a laugh-filled, tuneful musical to die for" (Variety) and "a cheek-aching laughter roller coaster - the most fun night out!" (The Daily Beast). Experience the "savagely funny (Time Out) pop-culture phenomenon that's been certified "hilarious" by The New York Times, Entertainment Weekly, Goldie Hawn, Beyoncé (!!) and countless fans on Instagram, TikTok, and beyond.
events.pleaseNote: No refunds or exchanges. Event date and time subject to change. All ages are required to have a ticket for this event. The Tennessee Theatre is not responsible for any tickets that are lost, stolen, or purchased through third party websites. Free parking available on weekends and after 6pm on weekdays in the State Street Garage behind the Theatre. For the safety of all patrons, all persons and items entering the Theatre are subject to screening by security officers and metal detectors. Prohibited items: weapons of any kind (including pocketknives), Illegal substances, cameras, audio or video recording devices (photo policy subject to change per event). Patrons who fail to comply will not be admitted into the venue or will be expelled from the venue without refund.

boxOfficeInfo.openHoursDetail: Monday-Friday 10:00am-3:00pm. Day of event - Will Call is available 1 hour prior to the start of performance
boxOfficeInfo.willCallDetail: Tennessee Theatre is a digital ticketing venue. The Box Office will be available 1 hour prior to performance to assist with ticketing needs.

venues.parkingDetail: Free parking is available for most night and weekend performances at the State Street garage located behind the theater, as well as the nearby Locust Street and Market Square garages. Additional parking lots and on-street parking are located nearby. For performances during regular business hours, parking is available in all of these areas for a fee. Parking fees vary from lot to lot. Please allow ample time to park.
venues.accessibleSeatingDetail: The venue has ADA seating in various locations. Please call venue Box Office for these. Venue has Elevators, and ADA Facilities, ADA Parking, ADA ramps and Entrance. For more info call 865-684-1200 ext. 2.

generalInfo.generalRule: Cameras, camera phones, audio, video and digital recorders, paging devices, and cell phones may not be permitted in the theatres based on the artists' policies. Guests using prohibited items may be ejected without refund.
generalInfo.childRule: All attendees, regardless of age, are required to hold a ticket. This applies to children who may sit on an adult's lap for the majority or entirety of a performance. For question, please contact the Box Office.

events.name: Broadway at the Tennessee: Death Becomes Her
events.info: Some people will do anything to look eternally fabulous. But famous actress Madeline Ashton and her best frenemy Helen Sharp are about to go too far... thanks to a mysterious woman named Viola Van Horn and a secret potion that's to die for. DEATH BECOMES HER is the Tony Award® -winning drop-dead hilarious new musical comedy based on the classic 1992 film with direction and choreography by Tony winner Christopher Gattelli. DEATH BECOMES HER is "a laugh-filled, tuneful musical to die for" (Variety) and "a cheek-aching laughter roller coaster - the most fun night out!" (The Daily Beast). Experience the "savagely funny (Time Out) pop-culture phenomenon that's been certified "hilarious" by The New York Times, Entertainment Weekly, Goldie Hawn, Beyoncé (!!) and countless fans on Instagram, TikTok, and beyond.
events.pleaseNote: No refunds or exchanges. Event date and time subject to change. All ages are required to have a ticket for this event. Tickets subject to cancellation if suspected brokering or violating ticket limits. The Tennessee Theatre is not responsible for any tickets that are lost, stolen, or purchased through third party websites. Free parking available on weekends and after 6pm on weekdays in the State Street Garage behind the Theatre. For the safety of all patrons, all persons and items entering the Theatre are subject to screening by security officers and metal detectors. Prohibited items: weapons of any kind (including pocketknives), Illegal substances, cameras, audio or video recording devices (photo policy subject to change per event). Patrons who fail to comply will not be admitted into the venue or will be expelled from the venue without refund.

events.name: A Christmas Carol (CBT)
events.info: Return to Knoxville's most cherished holiday tradition as Ebenezer Scrooge journeys through Christmas Past, Present, and Yet to Come in a dazzling celebration of redemption, generosity, and holiday spectacle.
events.pleaseNote: Children under the age of 4 are not permitted in the auditorium. A ticket is required for each person entering the performance. Only registered service animals are permitted, please call the CBT Box Office for seating arrangements. Additional accessible seating options may be available through the CBT Box Office, please call for additional accessible seating options. (865) 974-5161. Limit 6 total tickets per account. Tickets are non-exchangeable, non-refundable.
